channel.title: Brazil Elections 2026
channel.description: Real-time monitoring of the 2026 Brazilian presidential elections.

item.title: Desenrola 2.0: pessoas com salário de até R$ 8.105 poderão renegociar dívidas; saiba mais
item.description: The New Desenrola Brasil program allows individuals earning up to five minimum wages (R$ 8.105) to renegotiate debts from credit cards, overdraft, personal loans, and Fies, with discounts of 30% to 90% on principal and interest capped at 1.99% per month. It also permits the use of up to 20% of FGTS balance (or R$ 1,000, whichever is higher) to pay off debts, with funds transferred directly by Caixa to banks. The government will create a guarantee fund of up to R$ 13 billion (from R$ 5–8 billion in forgotten worker funds plus up to R$ 5 billion in new allocation) to shield financial institutions from default.

item.title: Governo lança ‘Desenrola 2.0’: programa prevê renegociação de dívidas e uso do FGTS
item.description: The government launched 'Desenrola 2.0', a program allowing workers to use up to 20% of their FGTS balance (max R$1,000) to renegotiate debts for those earning up to five minimum wages (R$8,105), with discounts of 30% to 90% on principal and maximum interest of 1.99% per month. The package covers families, FIES, businesses, and rural farmers, funded by a public guarantee fund of R$5–8 billion to back financial institutions. The provisional measure was signed by President Lula and will be published in the DOU today.

item.title: Zema defende limites para Bolsa Família: “Criamos geração de imprestáveis”
item.description: Former Minas Gerais governor and presidential pre-candidate Romeu Zema advocated for revising the Bolsa Família program, proposing limits on benefit payments. He argued that unrestricted social programs foster dependency, claiming they have 'created a generation of unemployables,' while acknowledging the program's importance for those truly in need.

item.title: Estudo realizado pelo TSE mostra distância entre população indígena e participação eleitoral
item.description: A TSE study shows that while 1,694,836 people self-identify as Indigenous in Brazil according to the 2022 Census, only 253,270 were registered as Indigenous voters by March 2026. The largest gap is among those aged 15 to 19, where only 32.6% of the Indigenous population in this age group is eligible to vote, indicating low electoral inclusion despite the youthful demographic profile.

item.title: Áudio: Lei regulamenta atividade do profissional da dança
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva signed Law 15.396/2026, which regulates the professional activity of dancers in Brazil, establishing rules for training, competencies, and employment contracts. The law requires contracts to specify working hours, place of performance, travel provisions, and additional pay for work outside the contracted city. The bill originated as PLS 644/2015 by former Senator Walter Pinheiro.

item.title: Próximos feriados nacionais de 2026: veja as datas e os pontos facultativos
item.description: After the May 1 holiday, Brazil's 2026 national calendar still has six national holidays remaining. The next national holiday is Brazil's Independence Day on September 7 (Monday), followed by Our Lady of Aparecida on October 12, All Souls' Day on November 2, Proclamation of the Republic on November 15, and National Zumbi and Black Consciousness Day on November 20. Additional facultative points include Corpus Christi (June 4-5), Federal Public Servant Day (October 28), and Christmas and New Year's eves (December 24 and 31).

item.title: Gonet vai atender o pedido de Gilmar para retaliar Zema?
item.description: The Attorney General's Office (PGR) is reluctant to comply with Supreme Court Minister Gilmar Mendes' request to include former Minas Gerais governor Romeu Zema (Novo) in the fake news investigation. Mendes, a former business partner of Attorney General Paulo Gonet at the Brazilian Institute of Education, Development and Research (IBEDP), has pressured Gonet to act against Zema, but PGR leadership resists, seeking to avoid the perception of personal retaliation.

item.title: STF não deve nem está em condições de rever decisão do Congresso de derrubar veto de Lula à Lei da Dosimetria
item.description: The Supreme Court (STF) should not overturn Congress's decision to reject Lula's veto on the Dosimetry Law, as legislative authority belongs to Congress and the Court had already endorsed the text during its debate. President Lula will let Senate President Davi Alcolumbre promulgate the law to avoid direct confrontation after the political defeat, although government allies plan to appeal to the STF to block the decision. The administration will not engage in immediate conflict with Alcolumbre but is considering nominating a Black female jurist to the STF to offset the political loss.

item.title: Flávio divulga DVD com ‘hat trick’
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) shared on social media a video edit showcasing his performance in a football match with allied parliamentarians, in which he scored three goals (a hat trick) while wearing a Vasco da Gama jersey, the team he supports. The post was circulated on his networks and highlighted by the site O Antagonista.

item.title: Zema diz que pretende rever Bolsa Família para evitar 'geração de imprestáveis' e impedir 'marmanjão' de ficar em casa
item.description: Romeu Zema (Novo), a pre-candidate for president, stated he intends to review the Bolsa Família program to combat fraud and prevent a 'generation of unemployables', criticizing beneficiaries who, he claims, prefer staying home watching Netflix and doing odd jobs instead of working. He proposes conditioning benefits on accepting job offers, allowing only one refusal, and warns of the risk of perpetuating informality and professional disqualification among youth.

item.title: A centralidade das lideranças comunitárias na disputa pelas cidades
item.description: The text underscores the centrality of community leadership in the struggle for just and democratic cities in Brazil, highlighting their role in popular organization, conflict mediation, and the collective construction of the right to the city, particularly in urban peripheries. Drawing on the MOTU experience, it shows that leadership is not innate but developed through practice, political education, and the articulation between daily life and structural struggles. Effective participation requires organized social bases, collective decision-making spaces, and continuous formation, challenging mere institutional consultation.

item.title: 3 dos 12 pré-candidatos à Presidência criticam as urnas eletrônicas
item.description: Of the 12 presidential pre-candidates in 2026, 3 criticize electronic voting machines and advocate for printed ballots, despite acknowledging the system’s security and audits. Aldo Rebelo (DC) defends maintaining electronic voting but suggests alternatives to increase transparency and reduce perceived vulnerability. Augusto Cury (Avante) considers the system secure and trusts it, but supports additional transparency mechanisms like auditable sampling, provided ballot secrecy is preserved.

item.title: Urnas eletrônicas completam 30 anos sob clima de desconfiança
item.description: Brazil's electronic voting machines turn 30 amid growing public distrust, with 43% of citizens expressing no confidence in the system, per a February 2026 Genial/Quaest survey. Despite three decades of operation without proven fraud, criticisms persist — particularly from figures like Bolsonaro and his allies, who were elected multiple times using the same system they now challenge. The TSE will hold a commemorative event on May 4, 2026, to counter misinformation and reaffirm the transparency of electronic voting.

item.title: Ao vivo: Lula detalha Desenrola 2, programa para reduzir dívidas
item.description: President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva launches Desenrola 2, a debt relief program offering 30% to 90% discounts on principal debt with interest capped at 1.99% per month, allowing up to 20% of FGTS use (if debt forgiveness is at least 40%) and banning online gambling for one year via CPF blocking. The measure will be sent as a provisional measure (MP) to Congress, taking effect immediately but requiring approval within 90 days. Desenrola 1, in 2024, benefited 15 million people and renegotiated R$ 53 billion in debt, but did not structurally reduce the debtor population.

item.title: Áudio: Congresso derruba veto e reduz penas para condenados por tentativa de golpe
item.description: The National Congress overturned the presidential veto on the Dosimetry Bill (PL 2.162/2023), reducing sentences and facilitating regime progression for those convicted of the January 8 acts, with 318 deputies and 49 senators in favor. Congress President Davi Alcolumbre stated that seven provisions were deemed prejudicial to prevent benefits for heinous crimes and criminal organization leaders, while government leader Randolfe Rodrigues did not rule out appealing to the STF, arguing that crimes against the Democratic State of Law do not allow for sentence reduction.

item.title: A nova derrubada de veto que interessa a Flávio Bolsonaro
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro is mobilizing opposition lawmakers to urge Congress President Davi Alcolumbre to convene a new session to overturn Lula’s vetoes on a bill that would include 22 Rio de Janeiro municipalities in the Semiárid region. This would extend the Garantia Safra benefit to family farmers in those areas, aiming to bolster Bolsonaro’s electoral support in regions where Lula and Eduardo Paes currently lead. The strategy frames Lula as opposed to rural producers and portrays Bolsonarism as defending farmers’ rights and local economies.

item.title: Flávio é Bolsonaro
item.description: Folha de S.Paulo faced criticism for referring to Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) only by his first name, 'Flávio,' in an article, which readers interpreted as an attempt to downplay his connection to former President Jair Bolsonaro. The controversy arose after the senator was mentioned as a potential presidential candidate in 2026, sparking debate over how the media treats political figures associated with Bolsonarism. The issue was widely discussed on social media and conservative outlets like O Antagonista.

item.title: Zema cita El Salvador e defende endurecimento no combate ao crime no Brasil
item.description: Romeu Zema, pre-candidate for president from the Novo-MG party, advocated for stricter public security policies in Brazil, citing El Salvador as a model for reducing crime. He stated that, if elected in 2026, he would implement tougher measures to combat criminality.

item.title: Charge do JCaesar: 4 de maio
item.description: The JCaesar cartoon published on May 4, 2026, offers satirical humor about President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, highlighting his political stance amid the 2026 electoral landscape. Part of VEJA’s political cartoon series, the illustration uses irony to comment on the current administration and its impact on public discourse.

item.title: Após reveses, Lula depende de Alcolumbre para aprovar pautas
item.description: The Lula government relies on Senate President Davi Alcolumbre to advance key electoral agendas, such as the 6x1 workweek PEC and the Novo Desenrola debt relief program, following tensions over Alcolumbre’s role in blocking Jorge Messias’ STF nomination. Alcolumbre, who is not running for re-election or Senate presidency in 2026, holds decisive power over government appointments and legislative progress, including the Security PEC. Without improving relations with him, the Planalto risks having its flagship initiatives stalled before the 2026 elections.

item.title: Polarização: pesquisa mostra quais sentimentos movem o debate eleitoral no X
item.description: The 'Network Barometer: Elections 2026' study shows that political debate on X (formerly Twitter) is driven more by negative sentiments—distrust (27.5%), skepticism (24.6%), and distrust in media (11.5%)—than by policy proposals. Anonymous right-aligned profiles, including the AI tool @grok, amplify polarization, with intense focus on figures like Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro, whose potential matchup accounts for 21% of mentions.

item.title: ELEIÇÕES 2026: FLÁVIO BOLSONARO DEFENDE REDUÇÃO DA MAIORIDADE PENAL DE 18 PARA 16 ANOS | NOTICIAS
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro advocated for reducing the age of criminal responsibility from 18 to 16 years old in a recent statement, reiterating a position long associated with his political circle. The proposal is part of a broader debate on public safety and juvenile crime in Brazil.

item.title: Lula quer renegociar R$ 120 bi em dívidas do Fies
item.description: President Lula launches Desenrola 2.0 to renegotiate Fies student loan debts, which have reached R$120 billion with 65.1% default rates, particularly in the North and Northeast. The measure aims to prevent collapse of student credit and comes ahead of elections, as young voters trend rightward.

item.title: Rejeição de Messias mela agenda no Congresso e racha STF em quatro
item.description: Senate President Davi Alcolumbre faced rejection after attempting to impose Jorge Messias' nomination to the Supreme Federal Court, triggering an institutional rift. Subsequently, Congress reduced sentences for January 8 rioters, affecting hundreds of thousands of prisoners nationwide, deepening the inter-branch crisis and generating profound, as-yet-unknown political and legal consequences.

item.title: Lula promete perdão a caloteiros em ano eleitoral
item.description: President Lula launched the second phase of Desenrola Brasil, offering partial debt forgiveness via a provisional measure in an election year. The program allows up to 20% of FGTS use, discounts of 30% to 90%, and caps interest at 1.99%, while banning online gambling for one year for participants. Although it aided 15 million in 2024, the program did not structurally reduce delinquency, which reached a record 82.8 million in March 2026.

item.title: Motta dá largada ao plano para emplacar prioridade de Lula
item.description: House Speaker Hugo Motta will launch daily sessions starting this week to fast-track the PEC ending the 6×1 work schedule, a top priority of President Lula’s administration. The move comes amid heightened tensions between the Executive and the Senate following the rejection of Jorge Messias’ STF nomination, with allies expecting Motta to adopt a more accommodating stance toward the government to secure passage in committee and plenary by the end of May.

item.title: Lula tenta mudar o foco após derrotas e avalia retaliar Alcolumbre
item.description: The Lula government faces two consecutive defeats in Congress: the rejection of Jorge Messias to the STF and the overturning of the veto on the Dosimetria bill, which benefits Bolsonaro. Privately, it considers retaliatory measures against Senate President Davi Alcolumbre, including dismissing his allies, while shifting focus to economic agendas like the Novo Desenrola and the 6x1 workweek reduction, which enjoys public support.

item.title: Lula quer perdoar até 90% de calotes em ano eleitoral
item.description: President Lula will launch the second phase of Desenrola Brasil on May 4, 2026, offering up to 90% debt discounts with access to up to 20% of FGTS funds and a one-year ban on online gambling for participants. The program targets credit card, overdraft, and personal loan debts, and includes the Fies student loan fund, which has R$120 billion in accumulated debt and 65.1% delinquency. Although 15 million were helped in the first round, delinquency reached a record 82.8 million in March 2026, with recent polls showing declining approval among youth, including 60.2% disapproval among 16–24 year olds according to AtlasIntel.

item.title: As três alternativas de Lula para o Supremo, segundo seus aliados
item.description: Five days after the Senate’s rejection of Jorge Messias’ nomination to the STF, Lula’s allies remain uncertain about the president’s next move, as he has offered no concrete clues about his new strategy. The subscriber-exclusive article highlights government uncertainty over how to respond to the defeat and which alternatives will be considered to fill the vacancy on the Supreme Federal Court.

item.title: STF avança sobre casos com impacto eleitoral e pode esvaziar atuação do TSE em 2026
item.description: The Supreme Federal Court (STF) is increasingly intervening in electoral matters, potentially undermining the role of the Superior Electoral Court (TSE) in the 2026 elections. Ministers such as Gilmar Mendes and Alexandre de Moraes have initiated actions against pre-candidates like Romeu Zema and Alessandro Vieira, which experts deem legally unfounded and possibly intended to intimidate critics during the campaign. This trend coincides with public criticism of judicial politicization and declining trust, with 60% of Brazilians expressing distrust in the STF according to an Atlas/Estadão poll.

item.title: O recado de ministros do STF ao Congresso sobre a derrubada de veto que beneficia Bolsonaro
item.description: STF ministers signaled to Congress that the Court should not interfere in the decision to override President Lula’s veto on the Dosimetry Bill, which reduces sentences for those involved in the January 8 attacks and benefits Jair Bolsonaro. The bill, approved in December and upheld in Thursday’s vote, was met with judicial indications of non-intervention, despite its direct political impact on the former president.

item.title: Gilmar pressiona Gonet para enquadrar Zema, mas enfrenta resistência na cúpula da PGR
item.description: Supreme Court Justice Gilmar Mendes pressured Attorney General Paulo Gonet to include former Minas Gerais governor Romeu Zema (Novo) in the fake news investigation, following a satirical post depicting Zema as a puppet. The initiative faces resistance from the PGR’s leadership, which questions its legality and proportionality. The case is politically significant as it involves a potential 2026 presidential candidate.

item.title: Aliados de Lula também veem erros de Messias na condução do processo que levou à derrota histórica no Senado
item.description: Lula’s allies acknowledge that Jorge Messias, the government’s nominee to the STF, contributed to his Senate defeat by pushing forward with the presidential message despite lacking solid support, overestimating backing from the opposition — particularly the evangelical bloc via André Mendonça — and aligning himself with a minister whose conflicts could destabilize the Court. His attendance at a dinner with an Alcolumbre rival and comments on the STF’s code of conduct were also seen as strategic missteps.

item.title: STF chega a sete meses incompleto, com dez ministros, sob risco de travar julgamentos, como o da eleição-tampão no Rio
item.description: The STF is operating with ten ministers after the Senate rejected Jorge Messias’s nomination, risking ties in votes, such as in the Rio de Janeiro interim governor case. That case was halted at 4-1 in favor of an indirect election by the state legislature but could reach a 4-4 or 5-5 tie, causing a deadlock. The vacancy also affects other cases, including the one on oil and gas royalties, which has been suspended since 2013.

item.title: Nunca, neste país, surgiu uma direita tão entreguista
item.description: The PL is expected to launch the candidacy of Deputy André do Prado for the Senate from São Paulo, with Eduardo Bolsonaro as a substitute, if the law allows. If elected, Prado could take a state or federal government position should Flávio Bolsonaro win the elections, allowing Eduardo Bolsonaro to inherit the Senate seat. The article suggests this strategy is part of a political maneuver aligned with the interests of Banco Master.

item.title: Governo Lula detalha novo programa de renegociação de dívidas; entenda
item.description: The Lula government will launch the new Desenrola Brasil program on Monday, targeting renegotiation of credit card, overdraft, personal non-consigned loans, and FIES debts, with interest capped at 1.99% per month, discounts of 30% to 90% on original debt, and the option to use up to 20% of FGTS balance for repayment. Aimed at individuals earning up to five minimum wages with debts overdue between 90 days and two years, the program will run for three months and include a one-year ban on online betting platforms for participants, as a response to gambling-induced indebtedness.

item.title: Governo lança nesta segunda novo pacote para renegociação de dívidas; veja o que já se sabe
item.description: The federal government will launch on Monday the New Desenrola Brasil, a package of measures aimed at reducing population indebtedness, allowing renegotiation of debts from credit cards, overdrafts, revolving credit, personal loans, and FIES, with interest rates up to 1.99% per month and principal discounts of 30% to 90%. The program covers incomes up to five minimum wages (around R$ 8,000) and permits the use of up to 20% of FGTS balance for debt repayment, with a one-year ban on online betting platforms for participants.

item.title: Quaest mede influência de governadores e ex-governadores recentes nas eleições estaduais
item.description: The April 2026 Quaest poll shows that 57% of Pernambuco voters believe Raquel Lyra deserves re-election, reflecting improved approval ratings (from 51% to 62%), though she faces strong competition from João Campos. In São Paulo, 54% say Tarcísio de Freitas deserves re-election, but the electorate prefers an independent profile, not aligned with Lula or Bolsonaro. Elmano de Freitas (CE) and Jerônimo Rodrigues (BA) are also seeking re-election, with scenarios ranging from consolidated favoritism to highly competitive races in other states.

item.title: Eleitor tem até quarta-feira (6) para tirar título e votar em outubro
item.description: Brazilian voters have until Wednesday, October 6, to regularize their electoral status, including obtaining a first-time voter ID, transferring residence, updating data, or registering biometrics. After this deadline, the voter registry will close for the October general elections, which will elect the president, governors, deputies, and senators. Voting is mandatory for literate Brazilians aged 18 to 70.

item.title: Lula inicia semana com expectativa de reunião com ministros para tratar de crise após derrotas no Congresso
item.description: President Lula faces a political crisis following the defeat of Jorge Messias' nomination to the STF and the overturning of his veto on a bill reducing sentences for those involved in the January 8 attacks, with allies urging greater presidential involvement to restore governability. The defeat was orchestrated by Senate President Davi Alcolumbre, allegedly with support from centrist parties and suspicion around Rodrigo Pacheco, drawing criticism of the government's congressional leadership.

item.title: Flávio Bolsonaro compara gols em pelada à vitória nas eleições
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ), a pre-candidate for president, posted a video on X showing himself playing soccer with opposition congressmen and compared the game to the October elections, saying he 'scored three little goals' and that the electoral victory will be 'like the victory hymn'. He emphasized unity as strength, stating that 'no one wins alone' and that with this 'wonderful team', they cannot lose.

item.title: Zema mira STF e acerta aliados em fala sobre “jatinhos” de Vorcaro
item.description: Former Minas Gerais governor and Novo presidential candidate Romeu Zema accused STF ministers of using their positions for personal enrichment and business dealings, stating that those who flew on planes linked to Daniel Vorcaro — imprisoned in the Master case — do not deserve public office. He tied the Master scandal to Brazilian impunity and the alleged dismantling of Operation Car Wash, claiming it allowed 'foxes' into the 'henhouse'. Zema also framed the 2026 election as a choice between 'untouchables' and 'honest Brazilians'.

item.title: Corinthians perde do Mirassol, vê fim de série invicta de Diniz e volta ao Z4
item.description: Corinthians lost 2-1 to Mirassol in the 14th round of the 2026 Brasileirão, suffering their first defeat under Fernando Diniz and returning to the relegation zone with 15 points. Mirassol’s goals came from Carlos Eduardo and Edson Carioca in the first half, while Dieguinho pulled one back for Corinthians in the 33rd minute of the second half. The result ended Corinthians’ unbeaten run under Diniz, dropping them to 17th place with one loss in seven matches under the coach.

item.title: Sou o único pré-candidato da direita do setor privado, diz Zema
item.description: Romeu Zema, the Novo party's presidential pre-candidate and former governor of Minas Gerais, stated he is the only right-wing pre-candidate with a private sector background, criticizing career politicians for relying on the public sector to solve Brazil's problems. He advocates for the privatization of everything, a fiscal plan projecting up to R$10 trillion in savings over 20 years, and argues that the public sector is often part of the problem, not the solution.

item.title: Zema quer rever Bolsa Família para evitar “geração de imprestáveis”
item.description: Romeu Zema, the Novo party’s presidential pre-candidate, advocates revising the Bolsa Família program to combat what he calls a 'generation of unemployables', proposing that beneficiaries who refuse a second job offer lose the benefit. He claims there are formal job openings available and that the Sine and municipal social assistance offices can help identify those who neither work nor study, criticizing the benefit as incentivizing informality and state dependence. Zema insists the program should be maintained for those truly in need, but fraud must be combated and the benefit should not perpetuate professional disqualification.

item.title: Zema defende alta de salário mínimo e aposentadoria pela inflação
item.description: Romeu Zema, the Novo party's pre-candidate for president, advocated limiting minimum wage and pension adjustments to the IPCA inflation index, opposing real gains above inflation. He also proposed an automatic trigger in pension reform to raise required contribution years as life expectancy increases, supported privatization of state-owned enterprises, and backed a regional minimum wage.

item.title: Ministros do STF usam cargo para “enriquecimento”, diz Zema
item.description: Romeu Zema, presidential pré-candidate from the Novo party, accused Supreme Court ministers of using their positions for personal enrichment and as a business negotiation table, advocating for their replacement via a joint nomination model between the Superior Court of Justice and the Federal Public Ministry, with a 15-year term limit and minimum age of 60. He stated that the continued presence of some ministers is unsustainable and that impeachment will occur naturally due to the Court's lost credibility. Zema also criticized the Senate for being passive in nominations and proposed limiting monocratic decisions to minor issues.

item.title: Zema defende que idade mínima para ministros do Supremo seja 60 anos: ‘Como um Papa’
item.description: Romeu Zema proposes setting a minimum age of 60 for Supreme Court justices, limiting their tenure to 15 years and framing the position as the culmination of a long legal career. He criticizes the president's exclusive power to appoint justices and suggests involving the STJ, Federal Prosecutor's Office, or OAB in the selection process, likening the appointment to a papal selection to prevent 'cronies'.

item.title: Líder do PL diz que crítica de maquiador a Flávio Bolsonaro foi conversa de salão
item.description: PL leader Sóstenes Cavalcante claims the criticism by Uruguayan makeup artist Agustin Fernandez against Senator Flávio Bolsonaro — alleging he fails to connect with lower-income groups — was likely a salon conversation taken out of context, possibly stemming from a vent by Michelle Bolsonaro. He denies Michelle encouraged the remarks but acknowledges Jair Bolsonaro’s absence from the campaign trail is causing disunity and weakening Flávio’s candidacy. Allies like Cabo Gilberto Silva insist Flávio is the official candidate and that internal disagreements are normal but should not drain campaign energy.

item.title: PETISTAS desesperados TENTAM ENTENDER como LULA está PERDENDO no DATAFOLHA em TODOS os CRITÉRIOS
item.description: Petty members express concern and confusion over Datafolha polls showing Lula losing across all criteria in 2026 election projections. The content reflects an effort to understand the causes behind his declining popularity, indicating anxiety within the Workers' Party. No specific candidates beyond Lula are explicitly mentioned.
